tools.name: draft_email
tools.description: Resolve recipients/attachments/account and return a preview. Does not send — the only tool that sends is confirm_send, and it must only be called after the user has seen this preview and explicitly confirmed.

to.description: Recipients. An array is clearest for several: ["alice@example.com","bob@example.com"]. One comma- or semicolon-separated string works too, as does "Name <alice@example.com>". Every address given lands in To — never move an extra recipient to cc to work around a rejection.

subject.description: Optional — a minimal default is filled in if omitted

body.description: The message body you compose. Plain text unless bodyType is "html".

attachments.description: Explicit file paths, glob patterns, or directories

recursive.description: Expand directory attachments recursively (default: top-level only)

account.description: Account alias; omit to use the only/default configured account

template.description: Optional message template key (see list_templates). Applies a subject prefix (de-duplicated) and a structural hint you should follow when composing. Use "fwd"/"reply" with the forwarded* fields for real quoted-block forwarding/replies.

theme.description: HTML visual treatment. "polished" wraps the body in a clean shell. Defaults to settings.emailTheme.

inReplyTo.description: The original's Message-ID, from read_email's messageId (e.g. "<abc@mail.gmail.com>"). Set this on a reply or the message arrives as a new thread rather than under the one it answers. Not the read_email `id`, which is a provider-local handle.

references.description: Full Message-ID chain for a deep thread. Omit and it defaults to [inReplyTo], which is correct for replying to a root message.

tools.name: list_templates
tools.description: List message templates (subject prefix + a structural hint you compose from). No args returns the core set; pass category, search, or all:true for more. Use a key as draft_email's `template`.

category.description: Filter by category (see the categories field)

all.description: Return the full catalog instead of just the core set

tools.name: confirm_send
tools.description: Dispatch the exact draft produced by draft_email — the only tool that causes mail to leave the machine. When alwaysConfirm is on (default), you MUST first show the user the draft_email preview, get their explicit approval, and only then call this with confirm:true; a call without confirm:true is refused and nothing is sent. Idempotent: re-calling with the same draftId after a successful send returns the original result.

confirm.description: Set true ONLY after the user has explicitly approved this exact draft. Required to send while alwaysConfirm is on.

tools.name: cancel_draft
tools.description: Discard a pending draft without sending.

tools.name: draft_campaign
tools.description: Prepare a personalised merge — N separate messages, one per recipient, each with only that recipient in To. Renders {{name}}/{{first_name}}/{{email}} per person and returns a preview WITHOUT sending. Use this when each recipient should be addressed individually and must not see the others; use draft_email when the message is genuinely collective and a shared reply thread is wanted. Refuses to draft if any placeholder has no value for some recipient.

recipients.description: Bare addresses (array or one comma-separated string), "Name <addr>" to supply the name inline, or objects {"email":"…","vars":{"name":"…","company":"…"}} for per-recipient values. The forms MIX freely in one array — pass plain addresses for everyone contacts already knows and an object only for the few who need a name. Names not given here are looked up in contacts.

subject.description: May contain placeholders. Required — a subjectless merge reads as spam.

body.description: The message, with {{name}}, {{first_name}}, {{email}}, or any custom token you passed in vars. Give a token a fallback with {{first_name|there}} — otherwise a recipient with no name on file makes the whole draft fail.

theme.description: HTML visual treatment. Defaults to settings.emailTheme.

account.description: Account alias; omit to use the only/default configured account

attachments.description: Paths/globs/dirs — the same files go to every recipient

ccFirstOnly.description: Cc attached to the FIRST message that actually sends, then dropped — how leadership sees the campaign went out without receiving N copies. There is no plain `cc` on a campaign; passing one is an error, not a silent no-op.

bccFirstOnly.description: Same first-message-only rule as ccFirstOnly, but invisible to the recipient. Use for an archive or a manager who should see the send happened without appearing on it. Rides the same message as ccFirstOnly when both are set.

throttlePerMinute.description: Send pace, default 20. Gmail app-password accounts have burst limits, and tripping one fails the rest of the run.

tools.name: confirm_campaign
tools.description: Send a campaign prepared by draft_campaign — the only tool that dispatches a merge, and it sends every recipient in one approval. You MUST first show the user the draft_campaign samples and warnings and get their explicit approval, then call this with confirm:true. Safe to re-call: it resumes a partially-sent campaign and never re-sends a recipient already marked sent.

confirm.description: Set true ONLY after the user has approved this exact campaign preview. Required while alwaysConfirm is on.

maxRuntimeSeconds.description: Cap this call at N seconds (default 600). Anything left stays pending for the next confirm_campaign call.

tools.name: campaign_status
tools.description: Per-recipient state of a campaign — who was sent, who failed and why, who is still pending. Call with no campaignId to list every campaign. This is how a partially-sent or aborted run is inspected before deciding whether to resume it.

campaignId.description: Omit to list all campaigns instead of detailing one

account.description: List view only — filter by account alias

tools.name: cancel_campaign
tools.description: Stop a campaign. Pending recipients become "skipped" and are never sent; recipients already sent are untouched and reported back — cancelling is not a recall. Takes effect between messages, so it also stops a run that is currently in flight.

campaignId.description: The campaignId returned by draft_campaign (see campaign_status)

tools.name: configure_account
tools.description: Add or update a Gmail account. The credentials are verified against Gmail (a live login) BEFORE anything is stored — a wrong App Password or stale OAuth2 refresh token is rejected here with VERIFICATION_FAILED rather than failing silently on the first send. The first account ever added becomes the default automatically. For oauth2, the refresh token must already exist — get one via the `mailman auth login`/`account add` CLI commands, which drive the browser consent flow this tool itself cannot.

alias.description: Short name for this account, e.g. "work". Re-using an existing alias updates it.

email.description: The Gmail address. One email = one account; a duplicate under a different alias is rejected.

method.description: How to authenticate: a 16-char Gmail App Password, or browser OAuth2

credentials.description: For app-password: { user, pass }. For oauth2: { clientId, clientSecret, refreshToken }.

setDefault.description: Make this the default account. The first account added becomes default automatically.

displayName.description: "From Name" shown to recipients, e.g. "Kalpesh Gamit"

signature.description: Appended to every draft from this account

skipVerify.description: Skip the live Gmail verification and store the credentials as-is (offline setup only). Default false.

tools.name: update_account_profile
tools.description: Update an existing account's "From Name" and/or signature without touching its credentials. Pass JSON null to clear a field, omit to leave it unchanged. Returns a signaturePreview (renderedHtml/renderedText) — show it to the user so they can verify the signature renders before it rides on real mail.

alias.description: Alias of the account to update (see list_accounts)

displayName.description: "From Name" shown to recipients, e.g. "Kalpesh Gamit"

signature.description: Appended to every draft from this account. May be plain text or HTML (e.g. a table-based signature pasted from a mail client) — declare which with signatureType, or it is auto-detected.

signatureType.description: How the signature should be read: "html" renders its markup on HTML sends (converted to readable text on text sends); "text" escapes it literally. Omit to auto-detect from the content.

tools.name: preview_attachments
tools.description: Resolve the same path/glob/directory input draft_email would accept and return the file list, without creating a draft or touching any account — a quick "what would this attach?" check.

attachments.description: Explicit file paths, glob patterns, or directories — the same input draft_email accepts

tools.name: list_accounts
tools.description: List configured sender aliases (no secrets returned).

tools.name: remove_account
tools.description: Delete a configured account. Requires confirmRemoval: true when removing the last remaining account or the current default — one ambiguous instruction should never silently leave zero configured accounts.

alias.description: Alias of the account to remove (see list_accounts)

confirmRemoval.description: Required to proceed when this is the last account or the current default

tools.name: get_settings
tools.description: Return current global settings — defaultAccount, draftTtlMinutes, alwaysConfirm, defaultBodyType, emailTheme, desktopNotifications and autoBccSelf. Read this before assuming a default; change them with update_settings.

tools.name: update_settings
tools.description: Update one or more global settings — default account, draft TTL, the confirm-before-send gate, default body type, HTML theme, desktop notifications. Only the fields you pass change; returns the full updated settings.

defaultAccount.description: Alias used when draft_email gets no explicit account. null clears it.

draftTtlMinutes.description: How long a draft stays confirmable before it expires

alwaysConfirm.description: Require confirm_send's `confirm` flag on every send (default true)

defaultBodyType.description: What draft_email falls back to when a call omits bodyType

emailTheme.description: polished = branded MailMan shell + IndiaNIC footer on HTML emails

desktopNotifications.description: Fire a native OS notification after each successful send (default true)

autoBccSelf.description: Bcc the sending account on every draft_email send so the sender keeps a copy (default false; skipped when already a recipient; never applies to campaigns)

tools.name: add_contact
tools.description: Manually add a contact to the local address book, independent of auto-populated recents.

email.description: Contact email address to store in the local address book

name.description: Optional display name for this contact

tools.name: remove_contact
tools.description: Remove a contact from the local address book.

email.description: Email address to remove from the local address book

tools.name: list_contacts
tools.description: Return the full local address book (no query filter), merged with Google Contacts for OAuth2 accounts — the "get my contacts" case.

account.description: Account alias; omit to use the only/default account. Determines whether Google Contacts are merged in (oauth2 accounts only).

tools.name: suggest_recipients
tools.description: Ranked recipient candidates for a partial name/email.

query.description: Partial name or email to match, e.g. "John" or "kal"

account.description: Account alias; omit to use the only/default configured account

tools.name: list_recent_emails
tools.description: List the most recent emails in a folder — "last 10 emails," "last 10 sent."

account.description: Account alias; omit to use the only/default configured account

pageToken.description: nextPageToken from a previous call — page further instead of raising limit

tools.name: search_emails
tools.description: Search a folder (or all mail) by query. oauth2 accounts get Gmail's native query syntax passed through verbatim (from:, subject:, after:, has:attachment, ...). app-password accounts get a simplified subset (subject/from/date-range) since IMAP SEARCH is less expressive.

account.description: Account alias; omit to use the only/default configured account

query.description: oauth2 accounts get Gmail query syntax verbatim (from:, subject:, after:, has:attachment). app-password accounts support a simpler subject/from/date subset.

pageToken.description: nextPageToken from a previous call — page further instead of raising limit

tools.name: read_email
tools.description: Read the full content of one email. id comes from a prior list_recent_emails or search_emails call. Attachment entries are metadata only — this tool does not download attachment bytes.

account.description: Account alias; omit to use the only/default configured account

id.description: Message id from a prior list_recent_emails or search_emails call

tools.name: schedule_send
tools.description: Confirm a draft for future dispatch instead of immediate sending. Persists to scheduled.json and installs the recurring OS ticker job if this machine doesn't have one yet. Must be called before the draft's TTL expires.

sendAt.description: Absolute ISO-8601 instant — resolve relative phrases before calling

tools.name: list_scheduled
tools.description: List pending (and recently resolved) scheduled sends.

account.description: Account alias to filter by; omit to list scheduled sends across all accounts

tools.name: cancel_scheduled
tools.description: Cancel a pending scheduled send before it fires.

scheduledId.description: The scheduledId returned by schedule_send (see list_scheduled)

tools.name: get_status
tools.description: Return the same structured data the `mailman status` CLI command renders as a tree — accounts, security state, and recent activity counts.

tools.name: get_mailbox_overview
tools.description: One-call snapshot of recent sent + inbox mail, with attachment name/size/type resolved for any message that has one (no attachment bytes downloaded). Returns structured JSON only — like every other mailman tool, rendering (a table, a colored dashboard, etc.) is Claude's job, not this tool's.

account.description: Account alias; omit to use the only/default configured account

limit.description: Per-folder limit, defaults to 10, capped at 50

tools.name: list_sessions
tools.description: Search this machine's past AI coding sessions by project, text, branch, or recency — the input to a session summary email. Returns metadata only (id, title, project, dates, size), never transcript content. Use projectsOnly:true first for a project roll-up, then drill in.

project.description: Substring of the project label or its absolute path, e.g. "mailman"

search.description: Free-text match on session title, project, and branch

since.description: Recency window: "24h", "7d", "2w", "3mo", or an ISO date

branch.description: Exact git branch the session ran on

limit.description: Max sessions to return (default 20, capped at 100)

projectsOnly.description: Return only the per-project roll-up, no session rows

refresh.description: Force a full re-scan instead of using the cached index

tools.name: read_session_digest
tools.description: Return a compact, secret-scrubbed skeleton of one or more past sessions (prompts, truncated replies, tool call targets, files touched, commits) — never the raw transcript. Ids come from list_sessions. This tool does NOT summarize; compose the summary yourself, then send it with draft_email.

sessionIds.description: Session ids (full or unique prefix) from list_sessions. An array, or one comma-separated string. Max 10 per call.

maxTurns.description: Turns kept per session before the middle is dropped (default 80, capped at 200)

includeTurns.description: Set false for facts only (files, commits, tool counts) — much cheaper
